name: NVIDIA A10
memory_bandwidth_basis: GDDR6 12Gbps effective x 384-bit = 600 GB/s. Bus width is the standard GA102 384-bit; the datasheet prints only the 600 GB/s aggregate.
notes: AUDIT CORRECTION: the dense/sparse flag on the tensor rows was inverted. FP16 125 / INT8 250 TFLOPS are the DENSE values (sparse = 2x). These rows were previously flagged dense:false, which wrongly told a reader they were sparse.  The stored numbers are correct dense values. Tensor figures are WITH SPARITY (sheet marks '*'): TF32 125 sparse / 62.5 dense, BF16+FP16 250 sparse / 125 dense, INT8 500 sparse / 250 dense, INT4 1000 sparse / 500 dense. FP32 31.2 is dense. A10 is GDDR6, NOT GDDR6X - do not assume the A10G/ workstation parts' memory here; A10G is a separate cut. 150W single-slot FHFL, no NVLink, no MIG, no FP64 Tensor Core path listed on the sheet (GA102 has no FP64 tensor path). Bandwidth is under 1/3 of H100 SXM at a quarter of the watts, which is why this generation's inference cards are memory-starved. No 'other' row: GA102 (A10) has no FP64 hardware path of significance, and the datasheet lists no FP64 figure.
